newsitem.title: USA: Judge rejects Harmony, N.J., eminent domain stance.
newsitem.headline: Judge rejects Harmony, N.J., eminent domain stance.

text.p: A Warren County, N.J., Superior Court judge on Friday ruled that Harmony, N.J., did not have the right to condemn a building financed by certificates of participation solely to force an early call on the debt, a lawyer involved in the case said.

Judge Harry Seybolt rejected Harmony's motion for summary judgment seeking to dismiss the lawsuit, and issued an opinion that said Harmony could not use the condemnation process for the purpose of calling debt early, according to Kenneth Laptook, an attorney at Wolff & Samson who represents the trustee on the COPs, the Bank of New York Co Inc.
Judge Seybolt was not immediately available for comment.
Phillip Gentile, a partner at Gentile & Turpen who represents the Harmony Board of Education in the matter, was also not immediately available.
Laptook said the judge invited him to file a motion to dismiss the case, or for the two parties to jointly dismiss the matter, since the central issue of the case had been decided.

The Harmony case had generated waves of controversy in the municipal market. Although many COPs indentures include provisions for an early call if the underlying property is condemned, debt holders argued that the provision does not envision an unnecessary condemnation solely for the purpose of calling debt early.
"This is good news for a lot of other people," Laptook said, referring to the other debt holders faced with unexpected calls.
The Pinelands, N.J., Board of Education has also attempted to use the technique, and the market responded with a rare boycott when Pinelands attempted to sell bonds last month.
